notes: Follow-up release that finishes the v1.0.34 brand sweep: drops the redundant "Terminal" subtitle that sat next to the ASA wordmark on every in-app surface, fixes the running-app's blurry taskbar icon (root-caused to a single-resolution favicon, not the embedded EXE resource), and adds light-mode wordmark variants so the dashboard's existing light theme renders the brand mark cleanly. No functional changes for the trading engine. This is a normal point release — both v1.0.34 and v1.0.35 share the `com.asasystems.terminal` Tauri identifier, so v1.0.34 users update via the in-app updater the same way every other point release lands. No manual install required. ### Brand - **Drop "Terminal" subtitle from in-app wordmark — product is now branded simply as ASA.** v1.0.34 paired the actual Copilot wordmark raster with a green styled-text "Terminal" word so the heading read "ASA Terminal" across the splash (`tray-app/src/App.tsx:104`), login (`templates/login.html:92`), dashboard sidebar (`dashboard.html:39` `Terminal`), onboarding (`templates/onboarding.html:60`), and admin (`templates/admin.html:65`) surfaces. v1.0.35 strips the secondary word from all five — the ASA wordmark IS the product mark; "Terminal" was a leftover descriptor from the v1.0.27→v1.0.31 "TradeSpace → ASA Terminal" rename. The Tauri window title (`tauri.conf.json` `app.windows[0].title`) and tray-icon tooltip (`app.trayIcon.tooltip`) keep "ASA Terminal" so the OS-level window-switching surfaces (alt-tab, taskbar grouping) still show the searchable two-word identifier; everything inside the app surfaces says just "ASA". Document `` tags keep the "ASA Terminal" prefix on purpose — that's the string that surfaces in the Windows alt-tab / taskbar window-grouping UI when the WebView swaps the host window's title, and the user explicitly wanted "ASA Terminal" preserved as the searchable window identifier even though the in-app brand simplifies to ASA. Historical CHANGELOG entries that describe the v1.0.34 wordmark are intentionally left as-is — those describe what shipped at the time, not the current state. ### Fixes - **Dashboard taskbar icon was blurry due to a single-resolution favicon, not a bad EXE icon resource.** User reported v1.0.34's running-app taskbar icon looked soft while the setup.exe icon stayed sharp. Diagnosis: extracted the RT_GROUP_ICON / RT_ICON resources from the installed `asa-terminal.exe` via a new `scripts/diagnose_icon.py` (uses `pefile` to walk `DIRECTORY_ENTRY_RESOURCE`) and compared byte-for-byte against `tray-app/src-tauri/icons/icon.ico`. Result: identical 7-frame multi-resolution set (16/24/32/48/64/128/256, all 32-bit BMP except the 256 PNG) — so the EXE resource is fine, and the blur is *not* coming from a winres-only-embedded-32px hypothesis. The actual cause: `dashboard.html:3` had `<link rel="icon" type="image/png" href="data:image/png;base64,…">` pointing at a single inline 32×32 PNG. WebView2 (Edge-Chromium) reads the page favicon and propagates it to the host HWND via `WM_SETICON`, where Windows then pulls it for taskbar / alt-tab / jump-list / thumbnail surfaces. With one 32 px source, every surface that asks for a different size (taskbar at 24 px, alt-tab at 48 px, thumbnail-preview at 96 px) had to scale the single buffer up or down — producing the visible softness. The setup.exe (a native NSIS dialog window with no WebView) reads the multi-resolution `installerIcon` directly, skips `WM_SETICON`, and stays sharp at every size. Fix: `scripts/build_icon.py` now mirrors a multi-resolution favicon set (`favicon-{16,32,48,64}.png` + `icon.ico`) into `static/branding/`, and all four HTML surfaces (`dashboard.html`, `templates/login.html`, `templates/onboarding.html`, `templates/admin.html`) declare the full set of `<link rel="icon">` tags so WebView2 has a native-resolution match for every taskbar request size. Verified post-build by re-running `diagnose_icon.py` against the new `asa-terminal.exe` and visually confirming the running-app's taskbar icon is now indistinguishable from the setup.exe icon at 100 % DPI. ### Brand assets - **Light-mode wordmark variants — charcoal A's on cream/transparent for light contexts.** v1.0.34 only shipped one wordmark raster (white A's, phosphor S, charcoal #080B0E background), which blended invisibly into the dashboard's dark sidebar but rendered as a hard charcoal rectangle around the glyph the moment the user toggled the dashboard's light theme. v1.0.35 adds four full-size variants in `branding/png/`: `wordmark-on-dark.png` (white A's, phosphor S, charcoal bg — mirrors the v1.0.34 default), `wordmark-on-light.png` (charcoal #1A1C1F A's, forest #0A4F2C S, cream #FAFAF7 bg), `wordmark-transparent-on-dark.png` (white A's, phosphor S, transparent bg — for placement over photography), and `wordmark-transparent-on-light.png` (charcoal A's, forest S, transparent bg — for placement over light imagery). All four are produced by `scripts/build_icon.py` from the same `wordmark-master.png` source via PIL pixel classification — three colour bands (white A's, green S, charcoal background) are identified by chroma, then re-coloured per variant with hard masks at full opacity so LANCZOS downscale produces clean anti-aliased edges. The dashboard sidebar gets a matching pair of cropped headers (`static/branding/wordmark-header.png` + `wordmark-header-on-light.png`) and `static/css/components.css` gains `[data-theme="light"] .sidebar .logo-row .wordmark-asa { content: url(...) }` so the wordmark swaps automatically when the user toggles `theme-btn`. Splash, login, onboarding, and admin surfaces are dark-only, so they keep the on-dark variant. ### Auto-updater note Same shipping pipeline as v1.0.30 → v1.0.34: PyInstaller `server.exe` sidecar → Tauri NSIS bundle → manual minisign with `npx tauri signer sign -f - -p ""` from bash (NOT auto-signer in PowerShell pipes — that produces 0-byte sigs) → SHA256 + UTF-8-no-BOM `latest.json` → `gh release create` → uploaded to `cjml34483/TradeSpace-releases`. v1.0.34 → v1.0.35 auto-updates cleanly because the Tauri identifier hasn't changed.
